implement.approach:
Defect on BASE (VERIFIED by reading + AC3 base run): supabase/functions/api/index.ts:4998-5004 `peekRateLimit('authfail', ip, 30, 300)` gates EVERY request by a flat per-IP failure counter, and index.ts:5016-5017 `recordAuthFailure = () => enforceRateLimit('authfail', ip, …)` charges that same per-IP counter for every 401 regardless of cause (junk bearer, expired token, dead session, wrong credential). rateLimit.ts:88/111 only offer scope+key windows, no notion of credential identity or refusal kind. Result: 30 refused requests from one handset behind a venue NAT → every peer on that egress (valid cached sessions, new bootstraps, refreshes, cache-expired sessions) gets 429 for the rest of the 300 s window. Round-4 (b133e4cb) replaced this with a NAT-wide `peekAuthStuffing` on every auth-cache miss inside authenticate(), which still fenced any never-cached bearer (adversary ATTACK 1-3).

Fix (rateLimit.ts, wired in index.ts): (1) refusal taxonomy `AuthRefusalKind = local | liveness | credential` — `authRefusalKind()`/`authErrorRefusalKind()` classify GoTrue error_code/msg (session_not_found, session_expired, user_not_found, user_banned, refresh_token_already_used → liveness; bad_jwt, bad_id_token, refresh_token_not_found, unknown → credential); 401s produced without consulting Auth (missing/malformed/expired-by-clock bearer, wrong issuer, deletion capability on a session route) are `local`. Refusals are tagged on the Response via `authRefusal()` and read back by `authRefusalOf()` so the handler's single `recordAuthFailure` charges correctly. (2) Per-credential shards keyed `ip:sha256(credential)` (`authFailureIdentity`) with the 30/300 s budget; a NAT-wide `authstuff` window keyed by ip is incremented ONLY on the first credential-kind refusal of a distinct credential. Local refusals charge nothing; liveness refusals charge only their own shard. (3) `peekAuthFailureBudget(ip, identity)`: a credential with NO refusal in the window always proceeds to Auth (so bootstrap-minted, rotated and cache-expired valid tokens are verified and served even under saturation); a credential already refused in this window is blocked on replay once its shard or the egress signal is saturated. (4) `chargeAuthFailure()` converts a NOVEL credential refusal into 429 only after Auth has judged it and the egress signal is already over budget — so an attacker rotating guesses gets 429s, never an unbounded stream of Auth-judged 401s, while every valid credential costs the attacker nothing and is never fenced. (5) The pre-Auth `peekAuthStuffing` gate from r4 is NOT present in authenticate(); refresh uses the refresh-token digest (request body) as its shard identity, not the bearer header.

Tests first (commit 934e20cc), then fix (commit 1b40f8f2). New suite rateLimit_nat_budget.test.ts (28 tests) pins: bootstrap-minted token first read 200 under stuffing; refresh-rotated token first read 200; valid session re-verifies at t0+601 s while stuffing persists (peer /auth/v1/user calls 1 → 2, response 200); attacker's replayed refused credential 429; novel refused credential converted to 429 post-verdict; local and liveness 401s never increment the egress signal; banned/dead sessions stay 401 without lockout; Auth outage stays 503; Redis- and memory-backed windows; concurrent charges. Three existing tests that pinned the flat lockout were replaced (not skipped/deleted) to assert the new contract.

residual_risks: Per-credential sharding means an attacker rotating distinct forged credentials is throttled only after each guess has been judged by Auth once (then 429 for further novel guesses while the egress signal is saturated); the per-IP pre-auth limit (1200/60 s) still bounds total Auth calls per egress. Sustained distinct-guess load therefore costs at most one Auth round-trip per distinct credential — a cost trade accepted so that valid peers are never fenced.

Refusal classification of Supabase Auth errors keys on GoTrue error_code/message strings; an unlisted liveness code defaults to `credential` (fail-toward-throttle for the guessing credential only, never toward locking out other credentials). Adding codes is a one-line change in rateLimit.ts.

implement.approach:
Defect on BASE (VERIFIED by reading + AC3 base run): supabase/functions/api/index.ts:4998-5004 `peekRateLimit('authfail', ip, 30, 300)` gates EVERY request by a flat per-IP failure counter, and index.ts:5016-5017 `recordAuthFailure = () => enforceRateLimit('authfail', ip, …)` charges that same per-IP counter for every 401 regardless of cause (junk bearer, expired token, dead session, wrong credential). rateLimit.ts:88/111 only offer scope+key windows, no notion of credential identity or refusal kind. Result: 30 refused requests from one handset behind a venue NAT → every peer on that egress (valid cached sessions, new bootstraps, refreshes, cache-expired sessions) gets 429 for the rest of the 300 s window. Round-4 (b133e4cb) replaced this with a NAT-wide `peekAuthStuffing` on every auth-cache miss inside authenticate(), which still fenced any never-cached bearer (adversary ATTACK 1-3).

Fix (rateLimit.ts, wired in index.ts): (1) refusal taxonomy `AuthRefusalKind = local | liveness | credential` — `authRefusalKind()`/`authErrorRefusalKind()` classify GoTrue error_code/msg (session_not_found, session_expired, user_not_found, user_banned, refresh_token_already_used → liveness; bad_jwt, bad_id_token, refresh_token_not_found, unknown → credential); 401s produced without consulting Auth (missing/malformed/expired-by-clock bearer, wrong issuer, deletion capability on a session route) are `local`. Refusals are tagged on the Response via `authRefusal()` and read back by `authRefusalOf()` so the handler's single `recordAuthFailure` charges correctly. (2) Per-credential shards keyed `ip:sha256(credential)` (`authFailureIdentity`) with the 30/300 s budget; a NAT-wide `authstuff` window keyed by ip is incremented ONLY on the first credential-kind refusal of a distinct credential. Local refusals charge nothing; liveness refusals charge only their own shard. (3) `peekAuthFailureBudget(ip, identity)`: a credential with NO refusal in the window always proceeds to Auth (so bootstrap-minted, rotated and cache-expired valid tokens are verified and served even under saturation); a credential already refused in this window is blocked on replay once its shard or the egress signal is saturated. (4) `chargeAuthFailure()` converts a NOVEL credential refusal into 429 only after Auth has judged it and the egress signal is already over budget — so an attacker rotating guesses gets 429s, never an unbounded stream of Auth-judged 401s, while every valid credential costs the attacker nothing and is never fenced. (5) The pre-Auth `peekAuthStuffing` gate from r4 is NOT present in authenticate(); refresh uses the refresh-token digest (request body) as its shard identity, not the bearer header.

implement.summary:
Defect on BASE ca928231 (VERIFIED): supabase/functions/api/index.ts:4998-5004 peeks one flat `authfail:<ip>` window before routing and index.ts:5014-5017/5039/5065/5071 charge it for EVERY 401 — Auth's dead-session (liveness) refusals, local refusals (no bearer, malformed, expired, deletion-capability misuse) and genuine credential failures alike — so 30 refusals from one NAT egress in 5 min answer 429 to every co-tenant, including VALID cached bearers, bootstrap and refresh. Because the mobile app's ONE implicit sign-out is a 401/403 refresh refusal (AGENTS.md) and 429 is retryable, signed-out handsets behind that NAT never learn they are signed out. rateLimit.ts:1-125 had no notion of refusal kind or credential identity.
